quiz.q: Dev database and API values are typed directly into the connector configurations, and the app is deployed to Prod. What happens?
options: Prod still connects to the Dev values — the wrong systems
Mule automatically switches to Prod values
quiz.explain: Hard-coded values travel with the code. Externalising them into one property file per environment fixes this.

quiz.q: What is the difference between `.yaml` and `.properties` property files?
options: Only the syntax — nested indentation vs. dot-separated keys; no performance difference
quiz.explain: The architect/organization chooses; the instructor even switched the demo to `.properties` and it worked the same way.

quiz.q: Where should the environment property files be placed, as a best practice?
options: In the project root next to pom.xml
quiz.explain: `src/main/resources` holds resources needed to run the project; a `config` folder keeps dev/uat/prod files together.

quiz.q: How should the Configuration Properties global element's File field be set so the right environment's file loads?
quiz.explain: A hard-coded `config/dev.yaml` always loads Dev. `mule.env` (name chosen by the organization) is supplied at deployment.

quiz.q: How do you reference a property in a connector configuration field such as the Listener port?
quiz.explain: `${key}` is used in configuration fields; inside DataWeave you use `p('key')`.

quiz.q: The `appid` query parameter is written in DataWeave (fx mode). How do you read the property there?
quiz.explain: `${...}` doesn't work inside DataWeave; use the `p` function with the key in single quotes (also written `Mule::p('key')`).

quiz.q: How do you pass `mule.env = prod` when running locally in Studio?
options: Run → Run Configurations → Environment tab → add `mule.env` = `prod`
quiz.explain: The variable name must match the one used in the global element; Mule then resolves `config/prod.yaml`.

quiz.q: You click the toolbar Run button directly instead of picking from its drop-down. Which configuration is used?
options: The configuration listed first/most recent — check which one it is
A new default with no environment
quiz.explain: The Must Remember point: toolbar Run/Debug use the first/most recent configuration.

quiz.q: Encrypting with AES and a short key like `xyz1234` gives "key length not sufficient". What does AES need?
quiz.explain: In class AES needed 16 characters; Blowfish accepted shorter keys. (AES accepts 16, 24 or 32 bytes.)

quiz.q: How is an encrypted value marked inside the property file?
quiz.explain: `![...]` tells Mule the value is encrypted; `secure::` is used when referencing it.

quiz.q: After encrypting the API key, the call still fails because the reference is `${weather.appid}`. Why?
options: The YAML file is in the wrong folder
Secure properties can't be used with HTTP Request
Without `secure::`, Mule uses the encrypted text as-is
quiz.explain: Secure values must be referenced as `${secure::weather.appid}` or `p('secure::weather.appid')`.

quiz.q: In the Secure Properties Config global element, how should the encryption Key field be set?
options: The key typed directly into the field
quiz.explain: Anyone with the code could decrypt secrets if the key were hard-coded; supply it at runtime alongside `mule.env`.

cards.back: Moving environment-specific values (host, port, path, keys, credentials) out of the code into one property file per environment, chosen at deployment.
`.yaml` (nested by indentation) or `.properties` (dot-separated keys). Only syntax differs.

cards.front: Same keys or different keys per environment?
cards.back: Same **keys** in every file; only the **values** change.
`#`. Use comment headings per configuration as a best practice. Ctrl+/ toggles comments.
`src/main/resources/config/` — e.g. `dev.yaml`, `uat.yaml`, `prod.yaml`.
1) File per environment 2) Configuration Properties global element 3) Reference with `${key}` / `p('key')` 4) Pass the environment at runtime.
Loads a property file, made dynamic with `file="config/${mule.env}.yaml"`. Path is relative to `src/main/resources`.
Variable holding the environment name (dev/uat/prod); name chosen by the organization; supplied at deployment.
`${key}` in configuration fields; `p('key')` (small p, single quotes) inside DataWeave.
Listener host/port/path and every connector config (HTTP Request, Database), including reconnection frequency and attempts.
Run/Debug Configurations → Environment tab → `mule.env` = `prod` (and `secure.key` for secure properties).
Readable → unreadable using a key and algorithm, and back.
Symmetric: the same key encrypts and decrypts. Asymmetric: different keys — more secure.
Adds the Secure Properties Config element (Add Modules in newer Studio; import from Exchange in older versions).
MuleSoft web page/JAR to encrypt and decrypt values: operation, algorithm (AES, Blowfish), mode (CBC), key, value.
16 bytes (16 characters) in class; shorter gives "key length not sufficient".
Marks an encrypted value in a property file.
Reads a decrypted secure property: `${secure::key}` or `p('secure::key')`. Forgetting it sends the encrypted text.
File `config/${mule.env}.yaml`, Key `${secure.key}` (runtime), Algorithm AES, Mode CBC.

cards.front: Why not hard-code the encryption key?
cards.back: Anyone with the code could decrypt the secrets. Pass it at runtime and never share it.
Ask the provider (preferably by email) for their Dev/UAT/Prod endpoints and keys; confirm mappings in writing.
